extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current ARR participants: reviewers, area chairs (ACs), senior area chairs (SACs), ethics reviewers, and venue program committees
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evaluative guidelines for participating in the ACL Rolling Review (ARR) process, including reviewer, area chair, senior area chair, and ethics reviewer responsibilities and timeline. Covers what reviews/meta-reviews should contain, assignment and availability rules, anonymity/formatting expectations, and the venue commitment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content and structure (what a review should do)
rubrics_metrics.description: A review should briefly state what the paper is about, highlight its strengths/weaknesses, and offer constructive advice to authors (regarding potential improvements) while signaling whether it merits acceptance in its current form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be well-justified. Reviewers should check appropriateness of the submission and its assignment to them. Reviews should include a brief summary, clear strengths/weaknesses, constructive suggestions, and an explicit signal about acceptability. Reviewers and authors are anonymous to each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of reviews per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission receives at least three reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR maintains a pool of qualified reviewers and assigns (at least) three reviewers automatically; ACs may adjust assignments if the automatic match is poor. If reviews are missing, ACs follow up and may assign emergency reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer eligibility requirements are defined in the Call for Papers (CFP) under Reviewing Requirements; researchers who meet these requirements may volunteer to be ARR reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers with sufficient publication records (e.g., as indexed in DBLP) may be added to the reviewer pool. Those who do not meet ARR reviewing requirements may still review workshops at organizers' discretion. See CFP for full eligibility details and how to volunteer (support@aclrollingreview.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer availability and load settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to each cycle reviewers indicate (1) their maximum reviewing load for new submissions (0 = no availability), and (2) whether they are willing to review resubmissions even if they indicated 0 availability for new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreeing to review resubmissions is encouraged to provide continuity of feedback. The site provides settings for max load/availability for each cycle (see 'How to Set Your Max Load / Availability for a Cycle').

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating reviews after author response
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should update their review as appropriate based on author-reviewer discussion (including the author response period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a designated author response window and reviewer discussion period; reviewers are expected to reconsider and, if warranted, update their reviews after seeing author responses and participating in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair role and high-level responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs (ACs, aka meta-reviewers) coordinate review of submissions: checking/refining reviewer assignments, coordinating reviewer discussions, and writing meta-reviews. ACs and authors are anonymous to each other. ACs know the identity of their reviewers, but not vice versa (by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should treat papers as submissions to ACL when evaluating them. All AC tasks occur through the AC console on OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chair in-cycle tasks (detailed duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: AC in-cycle duties include: checking for violations of submission requirements; checking and adjusting reviewer assignments generated by the matching algorithm; nudging reviewers who write low-quality reviews to reconsider and update; following up on late reviews and assigning emergency reviewers if necessary; encouraging discussion between reviewers before and after author response; and writing a meta-review with clear recommendations for authors and program committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should use the Area Chair tutorial and the AC console. For OpenReview issues contact tech@aclrollingreview.org. ACs may communicate via OpenReview comments/messages and use SAC help if needed to handle concerns or missing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review content and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews should summarize conclusions and provide clear recommendations for authors (regarding any important revisions) and for conference program committees (regarding whether it could be accepted in its current form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs are responsible for writing meta-reviews; treat papers as ACL submissions when making recommendations. Use Meta-review Form and Area Chair guidance to structure the meta-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC pre-cycle requirements and profile completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time ACs must complete a form indicating which areas they have the expertise to be an AC for and confirm that their OpenReview profile is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should keep OpenReview profiles up to date to facilitate COI detection and paper matching: include links to DBLP and Semantic Scholar, current affiliation, and current/past email addresses. Before each cycle ACs answer availability questions (max load and willingness to handle resubmissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: AC communication channels and anonymity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs can communicate with authors, reviewers, and senior members by posting messages (comments) in the OpenReview interface or by other methods shown in the Area Chairs' Guide to OpenReview. Reviewers are anonymous to each other (identified by pseudonyms) and do not see the identity of their AC by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slides and tutorials (Area Chair tutorial; Area Chairs’ Guide to OpenReview) explain how to contact reviewers and obtain email addresses if reviewers are unresponsive. SACs can also assist with communication issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Area Chair (SAC) duties
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs supervise areas: checking assignments of papers to ACs, monitoring and following up with ACs to ensure review steps are on track, assigning emergency ACs if necessary, and responding to AC questions about the process. SACs do not make acceptance/rejection recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SACs can communicate via email using the SAC Console or via OpenReview comments. ACs, reviewers, and authors are not told who their SAC is. SACs see identities of ACs and reviewers but not authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC ability to modify assignments and messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs can modify reviewer/AC assignments via the Senior Area Chair console ('Modify Reviewer Assignments' link and 'Assignments' view) and can message reviewer/AC groups from the SAC console.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAC Console preserves anonymity when messaging. If ACs or reviewers are unresponsive their email addresses are visible in the SAC console. See SAC FAQ and console instructions for step-by-step actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Some submissions are flagged for ethics review; Ethics Chairs coordinate and, if necessary, send papers to Ethics Reviewers who read the paper and offer supplementary feedback targeted at potential ethical issues. Ethics reviewing happens in parallel to regular reviewing, and ethics reviews are not shown to regular reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers can be flagged at any time, often via checklists ACs and reviewers complete. After flagging, reviewers and ACs should complete their normal review work without further consideration of the flagged ethical issues (ethics reviewers handle them). See the ARR ethics guidelines for specific criteria and examples and the guidelines for flagging papers for ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue commitment and program committee decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Venues (conferences/workshops) may subscribe to ARR and receive a pool of papers with completed reviews/meta-reviews for consideration (commitment). Venues set a commitment deadline and their own program committees decide which papers to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR is not customized to any particular venue. Venues enact their own decision-making procedures and communicate acceptance decisions to authors. Questions from venues about subscribing should go to the Editors-in-Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission anonymity and formatting limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All ARR submissions are anonymous and in the format of a short paper (up to 4 pages) or long paper (up to 8 pages). ARR reviewers are instructed to write a review as if the paper were being considered for the ACL conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ARR reviews are written with ACL in mind, low scores may indicate the submission is not a good fit for ACL even if appropriate for other venues. ACs check for violations of submission requirements as part of their duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and key deadlines for a cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Example February cycle timeline: submission site opens Feb 1; submission deadline Feb 15; withdraw without penalty deadline Feb 17; finalization of AC and reviewer assignments late Feb; reviewers receive/check assignments Feb 29; reviews due March 20; reviewer discussion and updating reviews around March 31-April 2; meta-reviews due April 7; author response and ethics review windows run in parallel; final reviews released to authors April 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission deadline is always the 15th of the month (other dates vary). There are additional tasks for first-time reviewers and simplifications noted (e.g., ethics process runs mostly in parallel). Exact dates vary by cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation that authors be willing to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of submissions are expected to be willing to review for ARR; researchers who meet the reviewing requirements and are interested should volunteer to the editorial team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being willing to review (and agreeing to review resubmissions) supports continuity of feedback. Contact support@aclrollingreview.org to volunteer; include the subject line 'ARR Reviewer Volunteering Inquiry'.
